<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 3823beb0dfabe1b5508653d832e1789f4a93e697 && git checkout 3823beb0dfabe1b5508653d832e1789f4a93e697

git fetch origin cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671 7f0c45b48d2f72e049c3ce4039c0552d0021ed43 && git checkout -B drift-repro cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671 && git merge --no-ff 7f0c45b48d2f72e049c3ce4039c0552d0021ed43
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cdd4eea93811522cca145a0f24858def51443671` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7f0c45b48d2f72e049c3ce4039c0552d0021ed43`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-trigger-params-shape.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts (the `type: 'flow'` arm, `executeFlow` and `endpointErrorAnswer`), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`handleAutomation`, `errorFromThrown`, the `dispatch()` catch), packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts (the action door's own `params` read, for flag ③-c), packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts and packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts (the `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` + `details.fields` derivation), packages/rest/src/error-response.ts (the transport's resolver call), packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts (the trigger route's declared request surface), .changeset/25821-trigger-params-object.md (prose face, read for ②)

Inputs: card #25821 body and its three comments (triage 6399814705, claim 6409382263, os-dev-report 6410469534); PR #25974 body, file list and the net diff `origin/main...origin/pr-25974` (merge-base `073f08b3`, three files: the changeset, `automation.ts` +61/-13, the new test +200); the check-runs on the head. Read-only: the diff was read with `git diff` and `git show` against fetched refs, nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**CI on the head is still in progress at review time.** 50 check-runs: 25 `success`, 15 `skipped`, 10 `in_progress` (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace), 0 failed. Concluded and green: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, the three card/branch/single-writer guards. The judgments below are read from the code; the in-progress families are the dev's reported local runs until they conclude (runtime typecheck + test 448 files / 7224 passed, dogfood 2523 passed, 69/69 dispatch-gate families exit 0).

**a. Which `params` shapes are now refused, at which doors — right.** `buildAutomationContext` (`automation.ts` line 156) now calls `objectValueFailure('params', ctxBody.params)` before any read. The function returns a failure for every value that is not `undefined` and not a non-null, non-array object: a string, number, boolean, array and `null` are refused; `undefined` (key absent) is admitted; an object, `{}` included, is admitted. Every door that reaches the builder gets the refusal, and I confirmed the caller set by `git grep buildAutomationContext` on the head: exactly two call sites, `respondToFlowTrigger` (`automation.ts` line 2172, reached by both `POST /:name/trigger` at line 3024 and the legacy `POST /trigger/:name` at line 2821 through the same function) and `executeFlow` in `endpoint-executor.ts` line 579 (every declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint). No other package imports the builder; the remaining grep hits are comments and CHANGELOG prose. The PR body's door table is accurate: the action door (`actions.ts` line 690, `reqBody.params && typeof reqBody.params === 'object' ? reqBody.params : {}`) does not share the builder and is unchanged; flow-to-flow nodes and MCP never pass through it.

**b. Refusing `null` matches the triage — right.** The triage's conditional ("and `null`, if the resume door admits it") resolves against the resume door's own loop on `main` (`automation.ts` line 3358 on `main`): `if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object' || Array.isArray(v))` pushes `invalid_type`, so the resume door refuses `{"inputs":null}`; `null` is therefore in the refused class, not the empty-bag class. Absent `params` (`undefined`) keeps the empty bag: `baseParams` is `{}` and the flat-body branch still runs, so `{}`, `{"ownerId":"u1"}` and no body at all build the same bag as before. One consequence the PR declares and I confirm is a real accept-set narrowing beyond the card's literal reproduction: `{"params":null,"ownerId":"u1"}` used to take the flat-body branch (`!ctxBody.params` was true) and run with `{ ownerId: 'u1' }`; it is now refused. Same for `0`, `false`, `""`. The changeset's Before/Now/Fix names this ("replaced by the body's other keys"), so the narrowing is declared where it is published.

**c. Accepted shapes are byte-identical — right.** `baseParams = ctxBody.params !== undefined ? { ...ctxBody.params } : {}` and `if (ctxBody.params === undefined)` replace `params && typeof params === 'object'` and `!ctxBody.params`. After the refusal above, `ctxBody.params` is either `undefined` or a plain non-array object, and on that domain the two spellings agree: an object (truthy) is spread and skips the flat branch in both versions; `undefined` takes `{}` and the flat branch in both. The `callerParamKeys`, `recordId`/alias seeding and identity envelope below the hunk are untouched. The test's six preservation cases on each route plus the endpoint case pin this direction.

**d. The resume door is byte-identical after the hoist — right.** On `main` the loop computed `received` with the arm-local `jsonTypeOf`: `v === null ? 'null' : Array.isArray(v) ? 'an array' : 'a ' + typeof v`. The hoisted `objectValueFailure` computes `received` as `value === null ? 'null' : Array.isArray(value) ? 'an array' : 'a ' + typeof value` and the message `expected an object (a map of names to values), received ...` with the same words; the pushed object is `{ field, code: 'invalid_type', message }` in the same key order. The loop's admission (`undefined` continues) and refusal predicate are the same truth table. The ordering around the loop (after the closed-set unknown-key refusal, before `resume()`) is untouched; `branchLabel` still uses the local `jsonTypeOf`, so that formatter stays local as its note asks. The ordering within the resume door and the outer `(body)` refusal are not in the diff. Judgment: no observable change on the resume door.

**e. The refusal body is the ruled one, before dispatch, no run row — right.** `validationFailure(message, [entry])` (`@objectstack/types`) builds an Error with `name: 'ValidationError'`, `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'`, `fields: [entry]`. On the REST doors the throw leaves `handleAutomationRequest` and `dispatch()` (the `dispatch()` catch rethrows anything that is not a permission denial, `http-dispatcher.ts` line 3170) to the transport, whose `resolveThrownHttpError` (`thrown-http-error.ts` line 208, called from `rest/src/error-response.ts` line 954 and `dispatcher-plugin.ts` line 739) maps a validation failure with no `.status` to `VALIDATION_FAILED_STATUS` (400), `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` and `details.fields` verbatim. This is the identical path the resume door's #9416 refusal already rides, so the two doors answer the same envelope. On the declared endpoint the throw is caught by `executeEndpointTarget` (line 648) and answered through `endpointErrorAnswer`, the same resolver, which the test asserts as `400` / `error.code === 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` / `details.fields[0] = { field: 'params', code: 'invalid_type' }`. The throw is before `automationService.execute(...)` at both call sites, so no run starts and no run row exists; the test pins `execute` not called on every refused shape at all three doors. Order on the doors is preserved: `flowIsUnknown` (404) and `flowStartRefusal` (403) run before the builder at both `respondToFlowTrigger` and `executeFlow`, so an unknown flow and a refused caller keep their answers before the body is judged, as the changeset states. The top-level message names `params` in backticks and the received type.

**f. Public surface.** No published schema moves: the spec's trigger route (`plugin-rest-api.zod.ts` line 1428) declares no `requestSchema` and describes the body as `{ recordId?, objectName?, params? }` with unknown top-level keys forwarded, which remains true. No `packages/spec/**` path is touched, honouring the claim's constraint. The client's `automation.trigger(name, payload)` is unaffected for every typed in-repo caller (all pass objects); a repo-wide grep for a trigger or automation caller sending a non-object `params` found none. The narrowing is of the runtime's accept set only.

**g. Test shape.** The new suite drives the real `HttpDispatcher` and the real `executeEndpointTarget`, pins both directions (9 shapes x 2 routes + the `null`-with-flat-keys case x 2 + 9 shapes on an endpoint refused; 6 bodies x 2 routes + 1 endpoint body accepted), and the PR records red-first (29 failed / 13 passed on base) and an ablation that restores the same count. Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25821-trigger-params-object.md`: `'@objectstack/runtime': patch`, title `fix(runtime)!: ...`, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing) — ...`, line-initial `Metadata-protocol: none (...)`, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, a BREAKING banner with Before/Now/Fix. The PR body carries the same two lines (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). Measured against the diff: the only published change is a runtime accept-set narrowing at the trigger doors; nothing a metadata author writes moves (no spec key, authorable value, stored shape or export changes), so `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right kind and under AGENTS.md's level rule and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ruling A (`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition) `patch` is the right level. The two cross-checks the gate refuses (`added` under `no`; `narrowed` without the `(narrowing)` arm) do not arise. The shape matches the two precedent changesets the report cites (25572, 25491: `patch`, `no (narrowing)`, `none`, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). Check Changeset concluded `success` on this head. The `(narrowing)` arm is what makes this contract review owed; `Clause-②: no` with the arm is the measured value, correctly departing from the claim's bare `no` (flag ③-a). Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: `[]`** in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- **a. Deviation: `Clause-②` declared `no (narrowing)` where the claim wrote `no`.** Answered: the measured value is correct (② above); the claim's line was pre-measurement, and the dispatch asked for the measured value. Accepted.
- **b. Deviation: `origin/main` moved after the pre-PR merge, head not re-merged.** Answered: at review time `origin/main` (`cdd4eea9`) is 14 commits past the merge-base `073f08b3`; `git log 073f08b3..origin/main` over `domains/automation.ts`, `endpoint-executor.ts`, `http-dispatcher.ts` and `domains/actions.ts` is empty, and `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/pr-25974` is clean. CI runs on the merge ref. Accepted; no re-merge needed for this review.
- **c. Out-of-scope class-a finding, the action door.** Confirmed in the cited code: `actions.ts` line 690 keeps `reqBody.params && typeof reqBody.params === 'object' ? reqBody.params : {}`, the guard this PR removed from the trigger builder, so `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action` on a `type: 'flow'` action still drops a non-object `params` silently (the report's live reading: `200`, paused run). Correctly left out: the #25821 ruling and the claim's file surface name the trigger door and the doors sharing its builder; the action door reads `params` itself. Escalated to the seat: file it as its own card (or dispatch it directly, per the owner's standing instruction on card handling), citing `objectValueFailure` as the ready check; the dev's dedupe strings are in the report.
- **d. Out-of-scope class-a finding, a non-object trigger body.** Confirmed in the cited code: `ctxBody = body && typeof body === 'object' ? body : {}` (`automation.ts` line 157) admits an array body (its indices are forwarded as params by the flat-body branch) and replaces a string body with `{}`; the resume door refuses a non-object body as `(body) invalid_type`. Correctly left out: the ruling covers `params` only. Escalated to the seat the same way as c.
- **e. The claim's `⛔ No packages/spec/**` constraint.** Held: the file list is three paths, none under `packages/spec`.
- **f. CI in progress.** The 10 in-progress families (Test Core x8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace) are the derived gates for the test and type surface this PR touches. This record judges the code; the seat lands only once they conclude green, per the Tier S rule (every check green beside the PASS record). No concluded check failed.
